pairs.question: Et quis est ille deus, qui concumbet mecum?
pairs.answer: Ille est Ammon, qui largitur divicias in omnibus.
pairs.derivation: Olimpiadis asks which god will lie with her; Nectanebus answers naming Ammon. Dropped the speech tags 'At ille dixit' (question) and 'Nectanebus inquit' (answer). Answer is the full single-sentence reply.

pairs.question: Et quam figuram habet?
pairs.answer: Neque iuvenis neque vetulus, sed in media aetate consistit habens in fronte cornua arietina, canos barbamque ornatam.
pairs.derivation: Olimpiadis asks what form the god has; Nectanebus describes him. Dropped tags 'Dixitque illa' and 'Cui ille'. Answer ends at the first full stop (after 'ornatam'); the following sentence 'Unde si tibi placet...' turns from describing to advising and is cut. Stripped editorial brackets around 'arietina', keeping the word.

pairs.question: Pater, hae stellae, quas tu computas, parent in caelo?
pairs.derivation: Alexander asks Nectanebus whether the stars he computes appear in the sky; Nectanebus affirms. Dropped tags 'dixit' and 'Cui Nectanebus'.

pairs.question: Et quam mortem debes facere?
pairs.derivation: Alexander asks Nectanebus what death he will die; Nectanebus answers he will die at the hand of his son. Dropped the framing 'Cui dixit'.

pairs.question: Dic mihi, quis es tu?
pairs.derivation: Nicolaus asks Alexander who he is; Alexander identifies himself. Dropped speaker frames 'dixit' and 'Cui ille'.

pairs.question: Cuius est hec statua?
pairs.answer: Statua haec Nectanebi, regis Egiptiorum, est.
pairs.derivation: Alexander asks whose statue it is; the Egyptians answer it is the statue of Nectanebus. Dropped 'dixit' and 'At illi dixerunt'.

pairs.question: O beatissime et pulcherrime certator, ut quid sine civitate?
pairs.answer: Magnissime imperator, antequam tu esses, habui civitatem, nunc autem per te civitatem non habeo.
pairs.derivation: Alexander asks Clitomachus why he calls himself 'cityless' (Sinecivitas); Clitomachus answers he had a city before Alexander but now has none because of him. Dropped the tags 'et dixit' and 'Clitomachus dixit'.

pairs.question: Quis ex vobis exiet luctans in ludo isto?
pairs.answer: Si placet vestrae potestati, ego recepta potestate pugnandi pugnabo et vinco.
pairs.derivation: At the Corinthian games Alexander asks who will come out to wrestle; Clitomachus volunteers. Dropped frames 'dixit Alexander' and 'Cui Clitomachus dixit'.
